newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA sees bigger Alberta ethylene plant.
newsitem.headline: NOVA sees bigger Alberta ethylene plant.

text.p: A US$600 million ethylene plant in Alberta planned by NOVA Corp and Union Carbide Corp would likely have up to one third more capacity than previously discussed when it came on stream, NOVA executives said on Tuesday.
The addition to the firms' Joffre plant in central Alberta, called EIII, was previously projected to have a capacity of two billion pounds a year when it started operations in the year 2000.

"I think the probability is very high that the initial capacity will be up substancially from that level," NOVA Chemicals president Dan Boivin told a conference call. "It's more likely to be between 2.5 and three (billion pounds)."

NOVA chief executive Ted Newall said the cost of the added capacity to the new plant would be borne in partnership with Union Carbide or alone by NOVA. But a third partner would not be brought in, Newall said.
"The reason that we'd bring it in at three billion initially, or 2.5...would be because we've got more customers than we have ethylene," he said.
